# Analytics services

## Quick map

| Service | Best for | Watch-outs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Athena | Ad-hoc SQL on S3 | Control scanned bytes; use partitions/Parquet; workgroups |
| Redshift | Warehouse BI, concurrency, materialized views | Cluster/serverless cost; dist/sort design |
| Glue | ETL, catalog, crawlers, DataBrew DQ prep | DPU cost; connector limits |
| EMR | Custom/long-lived big data stacks | Ops overhead vs Glue |
| QuickSight | Dashboards / SPICE | Not a general SQL lake engine |
| OpenSearch | Full-text log/search analytics | Hot/warm sizing + retention tiering |

## Comparisons

### Athena vs Redshift
- Choose **Athena** for infrequent SQL on data already in S3.
- Choose **Redshift** for repeated governed BI with tuning levers (dist, sort, MV, Spectrum).

### Glue vs EMR
- Choose **Glue** for managed Spark ETL jobs.
- Choose **EMR** when you need cluster-level control or frameworks beyond Glue’s sweet spot.

# Database services

| Service | Pattern | Exam cues |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redshift | Columnar warehouse | Dist ALL/KEY/EVEN, MV, Spectrum, federated, require_ssl |
| RDS / Aurora | Managed relational | Prefer over EC2 self-managed DB for patching offload |
| DynamoDB | Serverless key-value | TTL, streams, access patterns; not a lake SQL engine |
| MemoryDB / ElastiCache | Ultra-low latency KV | When microsecond-ish cache/KV is the requirement |

## Redshift distribution cheat-sheet

- **ALL:** small dimensions joined often
- **KEY:** large facts/dims joined on high-cardinality key
- **EVEN:** when no clear join key / avoid skew from bad KEY

# Security, identity & governance services

| Service | Role in DEA-C01 |
| --- | --- |
| IAM | Roles for Glue/Lambda/Redshift; least privilege; ABAC tag conditions |
| Lake Formation | Lake permissions, LF-Tags, integrating Athena/Redshift/EMR access |
| KMS | CMKs, grants for temporary decrypt |
| Secrets Manager | DB creds + rotation vs hard-coded configs |
| CloudTrail | API audit; query via Athena or CloudTrail Lake |
| AWS Config | Configuration change history / compliance timeline |
| Macie | Sensitive data discovery (often with lake governance) |

## Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store

- **Secrets Manager:** secrets with rotation workflows (DB credentials)
- **Parameter Store:** config and optionally SecureString; rotation story differs—prefer Secrets Manager for rotating DB passwords on the exam’s typical framing

# Storage & lake services

## S3 vs Lake Formation

| Concern | S3 alone | Lake Formation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object durability & lifecycle | Core strength | Uses S3 locations |
| Fine-grained multi-team access | IAM/path policies get complex | LF permissions / LF-Tags (TBAC) |
| Catalog integration | Via Glue Catalog | Governed catalog permissions |

## Lifecycle reminders

- Valid transition paths and minimum days matter
- Tag-based rules re-evaluate; untagging can prevent future transitions
- Restoring from archival classes is a separate operation

# Streaming services

## Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose vs MSK

| Need | Prefer |
| --- | --- |
| Custom consumers, shard processing, replay, enhanced fan-out | **Kinesis Data Streams** |
| Managed delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/HTTP with buffering & conversion | **Data Firehose** |
| Kafka ecosystem / existing Kafka apps | **Amazon MSK** |

## Lambda + Kinesis

- Default: shared throughput polling per shard
- Enhanced fan-out: dedicated throughput when consumers compete
- Batch window / batch size affect cost and latency tradeoffs

# Data Ingestion (Domain 1 · Task 1.1)

## Skill checklist

- Streaming sources: Kinesis, MSK, DynamoDB Streams, DMS, Glue, Redshift streaming patterns
- Batch sources: S3, Glue, EMR, DMS, Redshift, Lambda, AppFlow
- Schedulers: EventBridge, Airflow/MWAA, Glue schedules
- Event triggers: S3 notifications, EventBridge
- Lambda ↔ Kinesis integration, throttling, fan-in/fan-out, replayability
- Stateful vs stateless ingestion transactions

## Concept cards

### Silent under-production monitoring
- **Services:** Lambda, CloudWatch
- **Why:** Successful invocations can still write too few records; custom metrics + low-threshold alarms catch this.
- **Distractors:** Raising memory, swallowing exceptions, lowering concurrency.
- **Status:** verified (CloudWatch custom metrics pattern)

### Schedule vs event triggers
- **Services:** Glue, EventBridge, S3
- **Why:** Cron guarantees cadence; object-created events minimize latency for unpredictable arrivals.
- **Status:** verified

### Lambda default Kinesis consumption
- **Services:** Lambda, Kinesis Data Streams
- **Why:** Default mapping uses shared shard throughput; enhanced fan-out is opt-in.
- **Status:** verified

### Firehose vs Streams
- **Compare-with:** Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose
- **Why:** Streams for custom consumers/replay; Firehose for managed delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/HTTP with buffering.
- **Status:** verified

# Data Operations, Security & Governance (Domains 3 & 4)

## Domain 3 — Operations & Support

### Skill checklist

- Automate with MWAA/Step Functions/EventBridge/Lambda/Glue/EMR/Athena
- Analyze with Athena, Redshift SQL, QuickSight, notebooks
- Monitor: CloudWatch, CloudTrail, OpenSearch for log search at scale
- Data quality: DataBrew rules, Glue DQ, skew handling (AQE)

### Concept cards

#### Event-driven Glue failure handling
- **Why:** EventBridge on Glue state changes → Lambda; avoid polling GetJobRuns.
- **Status:** verified

#### DataBrew multi-column rules
- **Why:** Apply one check across many columns in a ruleset.
- **Status:** verified

#### Athena Spark vs always-on EMR for exploration
- **Why:** Burst exploration favors serverless notebooks to avoid idle cluster cost.
- **Status:** verified

## Domain 4 — Security & Governance

### Skill checklist

- AuthN: IAM roles, VPC SGs, Secrets Manager rotation
- AuthZ: least privilege, Lake Formation, ABAC (tag-based)
- Encryption/masking: KMS, TLS in transit, grants for temporary access
- Audit: CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs, Config for configuration history
- Privacy: Macie + Lake Formation patterns, sovereignty controls

### Concept cards

#### Secrets Manager rotation
- **Why:** Runtime secret retrieval enables rotation without redeploying hard-coded passwords.
- **Status:** verified

#### ABAC with project tags
- **Why:** Principal tags + resource tag conditions scale better than rewriting identity policies per project.
- **Status:** verified

#### KMS grants for short Glue jobs
- **Why:** Temporary decrypt permission without permanent key/role policy edits.
- **Status:** verified

#### CloudTrail + Athena for API forensics
- **Why:** Query existing org trail in S3 for DeleteBucket-type investigations with little new infra.
- **Compare-with:** AWS Config for configuration timeline (“what changed on this resource”).
- **Status:** verified
domains/data-orchestration.md:
# Data Orchestration (Domain 1 · Task 1.3)

## Skill checklist

- Orchestrators: Step Functions, MWAA, Glue workflows, EventBridge, Lambda
- Build for resiliency, retries, notifications (SNS/SQS)
- Serverless workflow patterns and timeouts/callbacks

## Concept cards

### Step Functions vs MWAA vs Glue workflows
- **Step Functions:** Serverless state machines; excellent for AWS service integration, approvals, waitForTaskToken; Standard for long runs.
- **MWAA:** Managed Airflow for complex DAG ecosystems, Python operators, multi-team data-aware scheduling.
- **Glue workflows:** Lightweight orchestration when the graph is mostly Glue crawlers/jobs.
- **Distractors:** Self-managed single EC2 Airflow “for simplicity”; cron-only for branching multi-hour graphs.
- **Status:** verified

### Callback timeouts
- **Why:** `TimeoutSeconds` / `HeartbeatSeconds` bound waitForTaskToken waits when workers crash.
- **Status:** verified

### Cross-account DAG triggering
- **Why:** Prefer dataset/data-aware scheduling over hard-coupled wall clocks across accounts.
- **Status:** community → verify against current MWAA docs when studying
domains/data-storage-management.md:
# Data Store Management (Domain 2)

## Skill checklist

- Choose stores: Redshift, S3/Lake Formation, RDS, DynamoDB, streaming stores, EMR storage patterns
- Catalogs: Glue Data Catalog, Hive metastore, crawlers, partition sync
- Lifecycle: S3 tiers/expiry, versioning, DynamoDB TTL, load/unload
- Models: Redshift dist/sort, Iceberg/open table formats, schema evolution, lineage

## Concept cards

### Athena vs Redshift
- **Athena:** Serverless SQL on S3; great for ad-hoc/infrequent queries; pay per data scanned.
- **Redshift:** Managed warehouse for repeated, concurrent BI with tuning (dist styles, materialized views, Spectrum/federated).
- **Status:** verified

### Lake Formation vs raw S3 IAM
- **Why Lake Formation:** Central governance, LF-Tags/TBAC, fine-grained access with less path policy sprawl.
- **S3 alone:** Fine for simple buckets; becomes brittle for multi-department lakes.
- **Status:** verified

### Redshift ALL distribution
- **Why:** Small dimensions joined broadly stay local on every node.
- **Distractors:** KEY on low-cardinality join keys causing skew.
- **Status:** verified

### Materialized views
- **Why:** Precompute expensive aggregates when freshness needs are modest (dashboards).
- **Status:** verified

### Partition registration
- **Why:** Prefer writing partitions into the Glue Catalog during ETL vs delayed crawler-only discovery.
- **Status:** verified

### S3 Lifecycle
- **Why:** Respect minimum days and valid class transition graphs; tag filters re-evaluate eligibility.
- **Status:** verified
domains/data-transformation.md:
# Data Transformation (Domain 1 · Tasks 1.2 & 1.4)

## Skill checklist

- Choose transform compute: Glue, EMR, Lambda, Redshift SQL/ELT
- Format conversion (CSV → Parquet), multi-source integration, JDBC/ODBC
- Cost optimization (Glue FLEX, right-sizing, partition pruning)
- Containers (ECS/EKS) when needed; LLM-assisted processing (Bedrock) where appropriate
- Programming practices: IaC (CloudFormation/CDK/SAM), CI/CD, Lambda concurrency, logging

## Concept cards

### Glue vs EMR
- **Compare-with:** Glue (serverless/managed Spark jobs) vs EMR (cluster control, custom frameworks)
- **Why Glue:** Daily ETL with minimal ops when features fit.
- **Why EMR:** Long-lived clusters, deep customization, multi-framework control.
- **Distractors:** Using EMR for tiny ad-hoc SQL; using Glue when OS-level bootstrap is mandatory.
- **Status:** verified

### Custom JDBC drivers on Glue
- **Services:** Glue, S3
- **Why:** Upload vendor JAR to S3 and reference in the Glue connection.
- **Distractors:** Lambda layers, support-case host installs, Firehose as JDBC.
- **Status:** verified

### Glue FLEX execution class
- **Why:** Lower cost for non-time-sensitive jobs.
- **Status:** verified

### Bedrock in pipelines
- **Why:** Classification/summarization via API from Lambda; not a metastore or Spark worker type.
- **Status:** verified

### IaC for pipelines
- **Services:** CloudFormation, CDK, SAM
- **Why:** Repeatable multi-account deploys with git history; still requires testing beyond syntax validation.
- **Status:** verified

# DEA-C01 Exam Overview

## Purpose

The AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate (DEA-C01) exam validates ability to implement data pipelines and to monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize cost and performance following AWS best practices.

## Target candidate

- About 2–3 years of data engineering experience
- About 1–2 years of hands-on AWS experience
- Understanding of volume, variety, and velocity impacts on ingestion, modeling, security, and storage choices

## Format (official)

| Item | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duration | 130 minutes | AWS certification page |
| Questions | 65 total | AWS certification page |
| Scored / unscored | 50 / 15 (unidentified) | Exam guide |
| Types | Multiple choice, multiple response | Exam guide |
| Passing score | 720 / 1000 (scaled) | Exam guide |
| Scoring model | Compensatory (overall pass; not per-domain) | Exam guide |

## Domains and weights

1. **Data Ingestion and Transformation** — 34%
2. **Data Store Management** — 26%
3. **Data Operations and Support** — 22%
4. **Data Security and Governance** — 18%

## Out of scope (examples)

- Performing ML training and inferences as a primary skill
- Language-specific syntax trivia
- Drawing business conclusions from data

## Study map in this repo

| Study file | Official coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `domains/data-ingestion.md` | Task 1.1 |
| `domains/data-transformation.md` | Tasks 1.2, 1.4 |
| `domains/data-orchestration.md` | Task 1.3 |
| `domains/data-storage-management.md` | Domain 2 |
| `domains/data-operations-governance.md` | Domains 3 and 4 |

## Q1. [examice] #1
*App id: `LOC-001` · type: `single`*

A data engineer is configuring an AWS Glue job to read data from an Amazon S3 bucket. The data engineer has set up the necessary AWS Glue connection details and an associated IAM role. However, when the data engineer attempts to run the AWS Glue job, the data engineer receives an error message that indicates that there are problems with the Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint. The data engineer must resolve the error and connect the AWS Glue job to the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet this requirement?

- A. Update the AWS Glue security group to allow inbound traffic from the Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint.
- B. Configure an S3 bucket policy to explicitly grant the AWS Glue job permissions to access the S3 bucket.
- C. Review the AWS Glue job code to ensure that the AWS Glue connection details include a fully qualified domain name.
- D. Verify that the VPC's route table includes inbound and outbound routes for the Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint.

**Answer:** D

**Explanation / Pembahasan:**

When dealing with VPC gateway endpoints for Amazon S3, it is crucial to verify that the VPC's route table includes the necessary routes for the gateway endpoint. This ensures that traffic intended for the S3 bucket is properly routed through the VPC endpoint instead of going out to the internet. Therefore, verifying and potentially updating the VPC's route table to include routes for the Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint is the correct solution to resolve the connection issue faced by the AWS Glue job.

Source URL: https://examice.com/exams/amazon/dea-c01#question-1

---

## Q2. [examice] #2
*App id: `LOC-002` · type: `single`*

A retail company has a customer data hub in an Amazon S3 bucket. Employees from many countries use the data hub to support company-wide analytics. A governance team must ensure that the company's data analysts can access data only for customers who are within the same country as the analysts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

- A. Create a separate table for each country's customer data. Provide access to each analyst based on the country that the analyst serves.
- B. Register the S3 bucket as a data lake location in AWS Lake Formation. Use the Lake Formation row-level security features to enforce the company's access policies.
- C. Move the data to AWS Regions that are close to the countries where the customers are. Provide access to each analyst based on the country that the analyst serves.
- D. Load the data into Amazon Redshift. Create a view for each country. Create separate IAM roles for each country to provide access to data from each country. Assign the appropriate roles to the analysts.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation / Pembahasan:**

The best solution for ensuring that data analysts can access data only for customers within the same country with the least operational effort is to register the S3 bucket as a data lake location in AWS Lake Formation. This service provides powerful data governance and fine-grained access control capabilities, including row-level security. By using Lake Formation’s row-level security features, you can easily define and enforce policies that restrict access to data based on specific conditions such as the country of the customer. This approach avoids the need for creating separate tables, views, or managing regional data migrations, thereby reducing operational overhead and complexity.

Source URL: https://examice.com/exams/amazon/dea-c01#question-2

---

## Q3. [examice] #3
*App id: `LOC-003` · type: `single`*

A media company wants to improve a system that recommends media content to customer based on user behavior and preferences. To improve the recommendation system, the company needs to incorporate insights from third-party datasets into the company's existing analytics platform. The company wants to minimize the effort and time required to incorporate third-party datasets. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

- A. Use API calls to access and integrate third-party datasets from AWS Data Exchange.
- B. Use API calls to access and integrate third-party datasets from AWS DataSync.
- C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to access and integrate third-party datasets from AWS CodeCommit repositories.
- D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to access and integrate third-party datasets from Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR).

**Answer:** A

**Explanation / Pembahasan:**

To minimize effort and time required to incorporate third-party datasets into an existing analytics platform, it is best to use API calls to access and integrate these datasets. AWS Data Exchange is designed specifically for discovering and subscribing to third-party datasets, providing direct and easy integration. This service effectively reduces operational overhead because it directly supports these types of integrations without the need for complex configurations or additional infrastructure. AWS DataSync, on the other hand, is primarily intended for data transfer between on-premises storage and AWS storage services, not for directly accessing third-party datasets through APIs.

Source URL: https://examice.com/exams/amazon/dea-c01#question-3

## Q5. [examtopics] #4
*App id: `LOC-005` · type: `multi`*

A financial company wants to implement a data mesh. The data mesh must support centralized data governance, data analysis, and data access control. The company has decided to use AWS Glue for data catalogs and extract, transform, and load (ETL) operations. Which combination of AWS services will implement a data mesh? (Choose two.)

- A. Use Amazon Aurora for data storage. Use an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster for data analysis.
- B. Use Amazon S3 for data storage. Use Amazon Athena for data analysis.
- C. Use AWS Glue DataBrew for centralized data governance and access control.
- D. Use Amazon RDS for data storage. Use Amazon EMR for data analysis.
- E. Use AWS Lake Formation for centralized data governance and access control.

**Answer:** BE

**Pembahasan:** Jawaban yang tepat adalah **BE**.

Ini soal pilihan ganda majemuk; kombinasi berikut memenuhi seluruh requirement:
- **B**: Use Amazon S3 for data storage. Use Amazon Athena for data analysis.
- **E**: Use AWS Lake Formation for centralized data governance and access control.

Konteks layanan terkait:
- AWS Glue cocok untuk ETL serverless, crawler/katalog, dan orkestrasi job/workflow.
- Lake Formation dipakai untuk tata kelola data lake, termasuk izin kolom/baris.
- Amazon S3 adalah object storage inti data lake; perhatikan lifecycle, partisi, dan endpoint VPC.
Kontrol akses fine-grained di data lake umumnya diselesaikan dengan Lake Formation, bukan hanya IAM kasar di bucket.

Mengapa opsi lain kurang tepat:
- **A**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Use Amazon Aurora for data storage. Use an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster for data analysis.
- **C**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Use AWS Glue DataBrew for centralized data governance and access control.
- **D**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Use Amazon RDS for data storage. Use Amazon EMR for data analysis.

## Q6. [examice] #4
*App id: `LOC-006` · type: `multi`*

A financial company wants to implement a data mesh. The data mesh must support centralized data governance, data analysis, and data access control. The company has decided to use AWS Glue for data catalogs and extract, transform, and load (ETL) operations. Which combination of AWS services will implement a data mesh?

- A. Use Amazon Aurora for data storage. Use an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster for data analysis.
- B. Use Amazon S3 for data storage. Use Amazon Athena for data analysis.
- C. Use AWS Glue DataBrew for centralized data governance and access control.
- D. Use Amazon RDS for data storage. Use Amazon EMR for data analysis.
- E. Use AWS Lake Formation for centralized data governance and access control.

**Answer:** BE

**Explanation / Pembahasan:**

To implement a data mesh that supports centralized data governance, data analysis, and data access control, the most appropriate combination of AWS services would be Amazon S3 for data storage and Amazon Athena for data analysis, along with AWS Lake Formation for centralized data governance and access control. Amazon S3 provides a scalable and cost-effective storage solution that is well-suited for large datasets, while Amazon Athena allows for serverless querying of data stored in S3 using SQL, facilitating data exploration and analysis without the need for managing infrastructure. AWS Lake Formation enhances governance by allowing the establishment of fine-grained access controls and ensuring data quality and compliance, aligning with the need for centralized governance in a data mesh.

## Q8. [examice] #5
*App id: `LOC-008` · type: `single`*

A data engineer maintains custom Python scripts that perform a data formatting process that many AWS Lambda functions use. When the data engineer needs to modify the Python scripts, the data engineer must manually update all the Lambda functions. The data engineer requires a less manual way to update the Lambda functions. Which solution will meet this requirement?

- A. Store a pointer to the custom Python scripts in the execution context object in a shared Amazon S3 bucket.
- B. Package the custom Python scripts into Lambda layers. Apply the Lambda layers to the Lambda functions.
- C. Store a pointer to the custom Python scripts in environment variables in a shared Amazon S3 bucket.
- D. Assign the same alias to each Lambda function. Call reach Lambda function by specifying the function's alias.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation / Pembahasan:**

Package the custom Python scripts into Lambda layers and apply these layers to the Lambda functions. Lambda layers allow for centralized management of shared code across multiple functions. Once the layer is updated with the new scripts, all the Lambda functions that use that layer will automatically inherit the updates, thus reducing manual efforts and ensuring consistency.

Source URL: https://examice.com/exams/amazon/dea-c01#question-5

**Answer:** A

**Pembahasan:** Jawaban yang tepat adalah **A**.

Opsi A paling sesuai karena: Apply a lifecycle policy to transition records to S3 Standard Infrequent-Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage after 30 days.

Konteks layanan terkait:
- Amazon S3 adalah object storage inti data lake; perhatikan lifecycle, partisi, dan endpoint VPC.
Perhatikan kata kunci optimasi (biaya/keamanan/skala) di stem; opsi benar biasanya menyeimbangkan requirement tanpa over-engineering.

Mengapa opsi lain kurang tepat:
- **B**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage.
- **C**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Transition records to S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage after 30 days.
- **D**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — Use S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage for all customer records.

## Q297. [github_examtopics_cache]
*App id: `LOC-297` · type: `single`*

Two developers are working on separate application releases. The developers have created feature branches named Branch A and Branch B by using a GitHub repository’s master branch as the source.

The developer for Branch A deployed code to the production system. The code for Branch B will merge into a master branch in the following week’s scheduled application release.

Which command should the developer for Branch B run before the developer raises a pull request to the master branch?

- A. git diff branchB master
- B. git commit -m
- B. git pull master
- C. git rebase master
- D. git fetch -b master

**Answer:** C

**Pembahasan:** Jawaban yang tepat adalah **C**.

Opsi C paling sesuai karena: git rebase master.

- **A**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — git diff branchB master

- **B**: tidak memenuhi constraint utama soal — git pull master
